mentl/23273fd:
RETRACTION FIRST. Commit 7e289435 claimed "the fix is half a fix" and
banked an address-to-node resolution gap that does not exist. That was
built on a mis-read: the probe addressed lines 14 and 16 of the fixture,
which are the BLANK LINES between the type declarations, and the module
placeholder is the correct answer for a blank line. A four-form control
probe refutes it -- every `type` kind resolves. Third mis-located
coordinate this session; the rule is to read line numbers off the
artifact, not off arithmetic.

THE REAL SECOND ROOT was the span. Every `type` form minted with the
bare `start` span -- the `type` token alone -- while FnStmt has always
minted span_join(start, body_span). The address resolver's line-mode
rule is "the widest node starting on this line", so a keyword-wide decl
node could never win its own line: `type Gain = Float where self >= 0.0
&& self <= 1.0` resolved to its own PREDICATE sub-expression and
rendered that node's unjudged t-var, while `type Bounded = Int where
self > 0` resolved fine for want of a wider constituent. That is why the
class hid.

THE FIX IS NOT A HELPER. A helper that makes the right span easier to
pass leaves the wrong one sayable, and nstmt takes the extent as an
ARGUMENT, so all nineteen mint sites each get to remember it. The type
family now does not: parse_type_decl returns its Stmt and parse_stmt
mints, because the dispatcher is the only thing holding both ends -- it
has the opening token and receives the closing index. Eight span
arguments deleted, one gained. span_last walks back over layout, since
the closing index sits one past the declaration and the predicate,
variant and row paths all return past a TNewline (which rendered a
source slice of a single `t`).

Measured: every declaration now slices its own text and speaks its
meaning -- `type Colour = Red | Green : Colour -- 2 variant(s)`, `type
Gain = ... : Gain = Float where 0.0 <= self && self <= 1.0`, `type Coeff
= Float repr f64 : Coeff = Float repr f64`.

or let-destructured tuples), it fell through to val_eq, which works
but with ~10 loads of indirection per call. Four load-bearing sites
named the string-equality effect explicitly:

  paths_contain (pipeline.lux, new)     — the member of the import
                                          dedup family that doesn't
                                          lie to itself about paths
  env_lookup    (ty.lux)                — the env is a List<(String,
                                          Ty, Reason)>; name matching
                                          is str_eq
  ctor_in       (lower.lux)             — constructor-name check,
                                          called per identifier ref
  name_in       (lower.lux)             — top-level-global check,
                                          called per identifier ref

The dedup fix is the headline: stage2 imports were being re-checked
6–8× because list_contains' polymorphic == never returned true across
dynamically-allocated strings. After: each module resolved exactly
once.

Plus closure-analysis wrappers gained list_to_flat at the entry:

  zip_params_to_env, bind_params_unknown_ty, collect_free_match_arms,
  collect_free_updates, collect_free_record, collect_free_stmts

per step post-flatten.

mentl/23df214:
The telemetry println in execute() fired on iteration zero of every
frame — `_icount` reset to 0 per call, so `_icount % 2_000_000 == 0`
matched at handler-dispatch frequency, flooding stdout. `lux wasm
file > out.wat` captured garbage until this was removed. With it
gone, compile_wasm on examples/wasm_check.lux produces 829KB of
clean WAT that wasmtime executes — the self-hosted checker running
natively on "let x = 42" through evidence passing across lexer,
parser, check, ty, and eff.

Also clears four pre-existing clippy errors gating the -D warnings
bar: drop `mut` from `args` in call_builtin_with_args (moved, not
mutated); collapse dump_to_rust's len-4/len-5 arms into a single
match (both slice from index 1); remove unused `Chunk` and
`HandlerTable` imports in dumper.rs; replace the no-arg `format!` in
the bootstrap wrapper with `.to_string()`.

Picks up rustfmt's pending reflow of dumper.rs and an alphabetical
`pub mod dumper;` ordering in mod.rs that had been sitting
uncommitted.

noodles/236dae0:
The transport's bpm is a TickParam whose timeline keeps every event
forever — by design, tick math integrates history — and setTempo fed it
rampTo(0.1), which setTargetAtTime expands into ~60 linear-ramp events
per call, Tone-side and native. Measured with a headless probe: one BPM
drag deposited ~48 permanent events and every dice roll 4 more; nothing
ever collects them. A drag moves 1-2 BPM per pointermove, so the glide
bought nothing audible: set the value directly (one event per distinct
tempo) and skip the write entirely when refreshAll re-pushes an
unchanged tempo after undo, key change, or a roll. The same probe now
measures 12 events for the drag that used to leave 45.
